Pick a stream and apply. We review your application, and if your background fits an open stream we reach out for a short screening conversation, then a briefing if it is a match. You build async to the brief, your room ships, and your fee is released against an invoice on standard contractor terms.
If we are not contracting for your exact area right now, strong applicants join our talent pool and we get in touch as soon as a matching room opens.

It is short on purpose. You will record a quick two minute intro video (this is required, and it helps us get to know you and how you explain things), share a few links that show your work, and tell us the areas you want to build in. # Customer Success Manager (Education)
## Our Mission
TryHackMe makes learning cybersecurity accessible, practical, and engaging for everyone. With more than 8 million learners worldwide, we're transforming how cybersecurity is taught; from school and university classrooms to professional training programmes.
## The Role
We're looking for a Customer Success Manager to own and grow relationships across our education portfolio. Universities, schools, and training providers are using TryHackMe to build the next generation of cyber talent.
This is a genuinely varied role. You'll manage a portfolio of around 150 accounts ranging from £2,000 to £15,000+ in ARR, working closely with an Account Manager who owns the commercial relationship and renewal and expansion process, while you own the customer relationship, activation, and success. Some of your accounts will need proper strategic engagement; EBRs, partnership-style reviews, and expansion-readiness conversations while others will move progressively into a lighter-touch, digitally-supported model as TryHackMe builds out its Education (EDU) digital motion. You'll play an active part in shaping that model as it evolves.
It's an exciting time to join: TryHackMe is investing in a new way of engaging EDU customers, and this role sits right at the centre of that change, giving you exposure to hands-on account management, digital programme design, and everything in between.
---
## Key Responsibilities
### 🤝 Relationship Management
For accounts with strategic value, expansion potential, or elevated engagement needs, you'll bring the full weight of a proper CSM relationship.
* Run EBRs, define success metrics, and lead strategic conversations with accounts where deeper engagement drives commercial outcomes.
* Build and maintain relationships with instructors, programme leads, and training coordinators.
* Work with the Account Manager to map the right stakeholders per account; the platform learners, budget holder, and renewal champion are often three different people.
* Ensure customers understand the learning outcomes their students are achieving and feel confident renewing.
### ⚙️ Digital Motion
* Contribute to TryHackMe's growing digital/self-serve motion for EDU, helping design onboarding journeys, lifecycle signals, and health scoring that let smaller accounts thrive without needing constant 1:1 attention.
* Oversee the digital experience for the lower-ARR accounts in your portfolio as this motion comes online, stepping in personally where signals flag genuine risk or opportunity.
* This is an evolving part of the role - you'll help define what "good" looks like as the model is built.
### 📥 Activation & Day-to-Day Support
* Own the customer relationship end-to-end; kickoffs, success plans, ongoing engagement.
* Respond quickly, accurately, and empathetically across email, Slack, and other async channels. Instructors are often in class and need fast, clear answers.
* Triage confidently - distinguish between configuration issues, user error, and genuine platform bugs.
* Escalate to support, product, or engineering effectively and follow through until resolved.
### 📈 Renewals & Expansion
* Partner closely with the Account Manager on renewals, acting as the eyes and ears on each account and flagging risk or expansion growth opportunity early.
* Surface renewal risk months in advance rather than at expiry.
* Identify and support expansion opportunities - new cohorts, growing usage, additional licences - on the accounts you own.
### 📊 Operational Excellence
* Keep HubSpot accurate and current, notes on every interaction, deal stages up to date.
* Monitor account health, adoption, and renewal performance across your book.
* Document what works so it can feed into scalable playbooks for the wider team.
---
## What Success Looks Like
**First 90 days:**
* Full portfolio reviewed, tiered, and any risks flagged.
* Strong relationships established with your key strategic accounts.
* Early activation gaps identified and being addressed.
**Ongoing:**
* Aim for 90%+ Gross Revenue Retention across the portfolio.
* NRR tracking toward 110–125%+.
* No renewal missed or deprioritised due to volume.
* A portfolio where larger accounts get genuine hands-on partnership and smaller accounts are well supported by an increasingly automated, self-serve experience.
* Clean, accurate CRM records at all times.
---
## About You
### ✅ Essential
* Experience managing a customer portfolio with clear renewal and retention outcomes.
* Comfortable moving between hands-on relationship management and a more systems-driven, digital approach. You don't need everything to look the same across every account.
* Strong data literacy - you use health scores, usage signals, and engagement data to guide your decisions.
* Excellent written communication - a large share of EDU engagement happens async, and clients can go quiet for extended periods (particularly over summer).
* Highly organised, with a reliable system for tracking renewals and flagging risk across a large book.
* A proactive communicator who's comfortable working cross-functionally with support, product, and sales.
* Confident running a genuine strategic EBR just as comfortably as supporting a lighter-touch digital account.
### 🌟 Desirable
* Experience in EdTech, L&D, or working with universities/schools.
* Familiarity with cybersecurity or technical training platforms.
* Experience with CS platforms such as HubSpot, Hex, ChurnZero, or similar.

## Understanding EDU Customers
Education clients aren't like standard B2B customers. A few things worth knowing before you apply:
* **Cohort and term cycles, not annual.** EDU clients buy on semester and cohort cycles rather than calendar quarters — renewal cadence and reporting need to reflect this.
* **Tokens, not licences.** Our EDU customers use a flexible token model, and you'll need to understand it well enough to explain it clearly.
* **Summer is a quiet period.** Engagement drops off significantly over the summer months - planning ahead for this matters more than reacting to it.
* **Live classroom constraints are real.** A platform issue during a scheduled class means an instructor standing in front of a room of students - speed and clarity of response matters enormously in these moments.
* **Curriculum mapper and content paths drive value.** These are core to the EDU experience, so strong product knowledge is important.
* **The stakeholder map is layered.** The platform learners, budget holder, and renewal champion are often three different people.
---

We hire people who care — about their craft, their customers, and our mission. Our most successful CSMs embody:
* **Ownership:** You act like a business owner; if not you, then who?
* **Speed:** You prioritise progress over perfection.
* **Empathy:** You care deeply about the learner and educator experience.
* **Resilience:** You're resourceful, persistent, and solution-oriented.
* **Craftsmanship:** You love refining your approach and setting new standards.
These align with our CS values of **Customer Empathy, Growth Mindset, Accountability, and Execution Speed**.
---

* 🌍 Fully remote & flexible hours (minimum 4 hours' overlap with UK timezone, 8am–6pm)
* 💻 Tech setup provided (laptop + accessories)

* 💪 £2,500 annual training budget for professional development
* 🧳 Annual all-company retreat
* 🍼 Enhanced parental leave
* 🍕 Virtual team lunches covered by us
* 🎟️ Free TryHackMe subscription for your friends and family
* 💰 401k / Pension plan
**Please note that, at this time, we are unable to provide sponsorship.**

3. **Take-Home Task** — Show how you'd approach a realistic EDU customer scenario.

We welcome applications from ambitious and innovative scientists to help develop next-generation biotechnology solutions for tackling PFAS pollution through artificial intelligence-assisted enzyme engineering.
An exciting opportunity to work as a Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) Associate has arisen as part of a collaboration project between Inspiralis Ltd and Cranfield University. Your role will lead the development of an AI-assisted enzyme engineering approach capable of designing and manufacturing tailored enzymes that can effectively break down PFAS pollutants, protect drinking water supplies, reduce environmental pollution, and support more sustainable and cost-effective remediation solutions.

Knowledge of artificial intelligence, machine learning, bioinformatics, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, or PFAS chemistry would also be desirable.
This role would suit an individual with excellent communication and project management skills, and the ability to work effectively across both academic and industrial environments. Previous experience of molecular biology, protein engineering, enzyme characterisation or related laboratory techniques is essential. You will hold a PhD, or be close to completion, in Biotechnology, Synthetic Biology, Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Bioengineering, Environmental Biotechnology, Chemical Engineering, or a related discipline.

The company is based at Norwich Research Park and has a multidisciplinary team of scientists and technical specialists, and it supplies high-quality enzyme products and services to customers across the UK and international life science sectors. You will work closely with Dr Nicolas Burton (CTO) and Dr Natassja Bush (CEO) and the Inspiralis team, as well as a multidisciplinary team of academics from EBIC at Cranfield University to develop innovative AI-assisted enzyme technologies for PFAS remediation.

## **Technical Operations Assistant**

### **Key Responsibilities**
#### **Pre-ship QA and hands-on testing**
* Carry out pre-shipment inspection and testing of chargers, accessories and related hardware using agreed checklists.
* Complete visual checks for damage, missing parts, labelling, configuration, serial numbers and overall presentation.
* Run basic functional checks, connectivity checks, app pairing checks or firmware-version checks where trained and authorised.
* Confirm the correct charger model, cable type, accessory pack, documentation and customer requirements before dispatch.
* Record QA outcomes clearly and quarantine any product that fails inspection or requires technical review.
* Escalate defects, repeat issues or uncertainty to the Technical Operations Manager before shipping.

* Assist with charger preparation, firmware checks, configuration checks and reset processes in line with written procedures.
* Ensure product labels, serial-number records and configuration information match the order or project requirement.
* Prepare any required product documentation, quick-start guides, installation notes or customer information packs.
* Support sample preparation, test units, demonstration units and replacement units when required.
* Maintain simple readiness records showing what has been checked, who checked it and when it was released.
* Keep the pre-ship QA area organised so products are clearly separated as pending, passed, failed or awaiting information.

* Pack chargers, cables, accessories and documentation securely and professionally for courier, pallet or collection dispatch.
* Book shipments and collections using the agreed courier, freight or supplier systems.
* Create and check shipping labels, consignment details, delivery notes and collection paperwork.
* Coordinate dispatch timing with sales, operations, technical support and customers where required.

* Maintain suitable packaging materials and advise when stock needs to be reordered.
#### **Collections, returns and stock handling**
* Arrange customer, installer, supplier or courier collections for returns, replacements, samples and test equipment.
* Receive inbound goods and check them against expected returns, purchase orders or collection records.
* Record returned chargers and accessories, including serial numbers, condition, reason for return and next action.
* Move goods to the correct location, including passed stock, quarantine, returns, repair, test samples and scrap areas.
* Assist with periodic stock checks and investigate simple stock discrepancies with the operations team.
* Ensure warranty, replacement and return items are handled carefully and records are kept up to date.
#### **Records, traceability and administration**
* Maintain accurate pre-ship QA records, dispatch logs, collection logs and product traceability records.
* Capture serial numbers, firmware versions, test results, photos or notes where required by the procedure.
* Update spreadsheets, stock systems, ticketing systems or project trackers promptly and accurately.
* File delivery notes, courier labels, collection confirmations and QA checklists in the correct location.
* Notify the relevant owner when orders are shipped, collections are booked, goods are received or problems are found.
* Support the improvement of simple checklists, labels and packing instructions based on practical experience.

* Follow manual-handling guidance and raise concerns if items, pallets or packaging require additional support.

## Why Verifone
For more than 40 years Verifone has established a remarkable record of leadership in the electronic payment technology industry. Verifone has one of the leading electronic payment solutions brands and is one of the largest providers of electronic payment systems worldwide.
Verifone has a diverse, dynamic and fast paced work environment in which employees are focused on results and have opportunities to excel. We take pride in the fact that we work with leading retailers, merchants, banks, and third party partners to invent and deliver innovative payments solution around the world. We strive for excellence in our products and services, and are obsessed with customer happiness. Across the globe, Verifone employees are leading the payments industry through experience, innovation, and an ambitious spirit. Whether it’s developing the next platform of secure payment systems or searching for new ways to bring electronic payments to new markets, the team at Verifone is dedicated to the success of our customers, partners and investors. It is this passion for innovation that drives each one of our employees for personal and professional success.
Verifone is proudly an in-office work culture as we see immense benefits to career development and business results from our colleagues being physically co-located. Currently, we do allow a hybrid work schedule but we regularly revisit our attendance policy.
## About The Role
The **EMEA Scheme Compliance Manager – Acquiring** ensures Verifone’s acquiring and gateway solutions remain fully compliant with Visa, Mastercard, and other payment scheme requirements. This role translates scheme mandates into clear internal deliverables, manages non‐compliance risk, and acts as Verifone’s primary point of contact with regional scheme partners. It is a cross‐functional role spanning Product, Engineering, Finance, Certification, Customer Success, and Sales.
**Key Responsibilities:**
**Scheme Mandate & Release Management**
* Monitor Visa/Mastercard bi‐annual releases, mandates, and scheme bulletins; summarise and distribute requirements to internal teams.
* Translate scheme changes into internal requirements and submit prioritised items into relevant Product backlogs.
* Track EMEA mandate deadlines and escalate delivery risks.
* Manage acquirer/processor‐initiated changes related to scheme mandates.
* Drive mandate delivery through to GTM in partnership with Product Owners and Customer Success.
**Non‐Compliance & Risk Management**
* Track non‐compliance notifications from Visa, Mastercard, Amex, and Discover.
* Identify root causes and define remediation requirements; ensure timely resolution.
* Support scheme fraud investigations for EMEA acquiring customers.
* Maintain visibility of fines, remediation progress, and compliance status through dashboards and regular reporting.
**Scheme Reporting & Fee Governance**
* Complete mandatory scheme reporting for EMEA acquiring entities.

Job Title: Health & Safety Lead, Development Location: London
Job Summary: Join a team defining the future of safe, sustainable, high-performance data infrastructure projects. As our Development Health & Safety Lead, you will champion and be responsible for safety, compliance, and risk mitigation across the entire capital project lifecycle, from design, initial ground-breaking and civil works through to structural build, MEP installation, and testing & commissioning. Your primary mission is to embed a world-class safety culture across our development sites, ensuring all projects are delivered entirely incident-free. What we are looking for: A degree educated professional with a proven track record in the delivery of large scale commercial or industrial projects with international workforces. With a passion for continuous improvement in all aspects of EHS within and outside projects, who can demonstrate extensive hands-on experience managing large-scale build safety for critical infrastructure, or heavy industrial developments. Policy/Project Planning and Risk Management: * Develop and implement construction EHS policies, project safety plans, and field procedures to ensure compliance with Verne and customer standards.
* Oversee project hazard analyses, risk assessments, and regular site inspections to proactively identify and mitigate safety concerns.
* Review, optimize and enforce strict risk mitigation strategies specific to high-risk build activities, including heavy lifting operations, structural works, working at heights, excavation works, temporary works and commissioning works.
Regulatory Compliance: * Ensure strict adherence to all local construction regulations and relevant EU safety directives.
* Manage the tracking, and ongoing maintenance of all essential construction-related H&S permits, environmental licenses, and project documentation.
* Serve as the primary point of contact for external regulatory bodies during construction site inspections, audits, and official inquiries.
* Demonstrate strong working knowledge of ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 management systems within a capital project delivery context.
Incident Management & Prevention: * Provide end-to-end construction incident management support, leading comprehensive investigations for all on-site accidents, near-misses, and safety observations alongside local teams and principal contractors.
* Conduct thorough Root Cause Analyses reports and partner with engineering and construction teams to implement and track robust Corrective and Preventative Actions (CAPA) to full closure.
Training & Safety Culture: * Working with project stakeholders, design, deliver, and continuously optimize construction site EHS inductions, specialized safety briefings, and toolbox talk frameworks.
* Foster a proactive, No-Blame behavioural safety culture on site rooted in transparent reporting, empowering every contractor and worker with Stop Work Authority.
* Coordinate on-site construction safety committees and align project leadership with field safety representatives.
Contractor & Vendor Safety: * Lead the safety pre-qualification, review, and approval process for principal contractors, vendors, and specialized construction partners.
* Audit and approve contractor Construction Phase Plans, where applicable RAMS and site-specific Permit-to-Work protocols.
* Enforce strict competency and training verification gates for all on-site construction personnel and contractors before works commence.
* Conduct regular safety walks, behavioural safety audits, and formal evaluations of contractor activities to maintain an uncompromising standard of site safety.
* Operational handover
* Lead the safety component of the testing, commissioning, and final handover phases, ensuring a clean, thoroughly documented transition to the Operations team.
Required Qualifications: * Bachelor's degree in occupational health & safety or higher.
* Bolt on additional EHS qualifications.
* 10+ years of progressive EHS leadership experience within large-scale industrial construction, hyperscale data centre builds, high-tech manufacturing developments, or critical infrastructure projects.
* Deep understanding of construction safety laws, example CDM 2015 (UK) and wider EU/Nordic construction health and safety directives etc.

Join our team at the Guardian and be a part of a diverse and inclusive global
organisation that delivers fearless, investigative journalism, and holds power
to account. Our team of award-winning journalists, cutting-edge commercial
professionals, and industry-leading digital experts are committed to making a
difference and represent a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. We offer
a challenging and exciting environment for career development, with a focus on
training, growth and fostering an inclusive culture.
 
We are now looking for a Senior Android Developer to join our growing Apps
Experience team. Development of digital products is central to the Guardian. We
create our award-winning Android app primarily in Kotlin and Java using Android
Studio. We're focussed on providing a fast and stable experience to our users,
and our Play Store rating of 4.7 stars is testament to that.
 
You'll work on major new features, as well as improving and maintaining existing
functionality for The Guardian’s Android apps. As a Senior Developer you’ll take
the lead on projects and offer encouragement and guidance to help others to
grow. 
 
About the role
 
* Building and testing major new features, as well as improving and maintaining
existing functionality for our apps.
* Working  90%+ in Kotlin, but you may be required to work with Java too.
* You won't be coding in isolation - our culture is strongly collaborative,
whether pair programming with other developers or working closely with other
stakeholders. 
* You can expect to work closely with iOS, server-side, and web engineers, and
designers, product managers, editorial and commercial colleagues.
* You'll take on a leadership role in some of the teams projects
* You’ll be encouraged to help others grow - you will pass on your expertise to
other developers, whilst continuing to grow yourself.
* Sometimes deciding what code to write is as hard as writing the code itself.
As an engineer you'll be involved in product decisions as well as technical
ones.
* You'll strive to be innovative on a daily basis, as well as at our regular
hack days.
 
About you
 
* You have demonstrated expertise in Android development and you have a strong
interest in growing your skills.
* You have strong competence in one or more of modern Android development
tools, including Jetpack Compose, Coroutines/Flow, MVVM, Webviews, other
Jetpack libraries, and modular app architectures.
* You test your code and promote a culture of testing. Demonstrate experience
with some of JVM unit testing, instrumented testing, and UI regression
testing
* You are comfortable working with both cutting edge technologies as well as
legacy code
* You have experience of, or are willing to take on a leadership role in some
team projects
* You have a rough idea of how iOS development works and you'd like to know
more, perhaps even try it yourself.
* Familiarity with Swift and ObjectiveC for iOS, or Scala and Typescript for
server side development is useful. 
 
We actively encourage applications from groups traditionally underrepresented in
the UK media
 
Our developers operate in a hybrid environment working 1 day a week from our
offices in Kings Cross and 4 days remotely. If you’d like to come in more than
that, that’s great too. 
 
We strive for transparency in remuneration where possible. The salary for new
Senior Android Developers at the Guardian is £82,000 per year. 
 
We value and respect all differences (seen and unseen) in all people. We aspire
to have inclusive working experiences and an environment that reflects the
audience we serve, where our people have equal access to career development
opportunities, their voices are heard and can contribute to our future. We
actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. Many of our
staff work flexibly and we will consider all requests for flexible working
arrangements.
 
How to apply
 
To apply, please upload your latest CV. We don’t require a cover letter but
we’ll ask you a question about android development as part of the application
questionnaire. This question should take no longer than 5 minutes to answer, so
please factor in the extra time when applying. 
 
We appreciate the time taken to prepare each application we receive. We do not
use AI-assisted technology to review applications; every application is reviewed
by a member of our recruitment team. Thank you for bearing with us during the
screening process. 
 
The closing date for applications is Friday 7th August 2026.
 
All roles at the Guardian are open for everybody to apply. It is important to us
that you feel supported and comfortable throughout your recruitment process, in
order to perform your best. Please let us know if there are any changes we could
make to help your application, this includes providing documents in accessible
formats or personalising the process to better support your needs. Please
contact Anna Vipers on anna.vipers@theguardian.com to discuss further so we can
work with you to support you through your application.
 
Benefits at the Guardian
You'll have 30 days of annual leave per year (plus bank holidays) with the
option to purchase an additional 5 days. Our pension scheme is generous; if you
contribute 5% then we will contribute 8-12% (depending on your age). We believe
in giving back, which is why employees are given 2 volunteering days annually
and the option of payroll giving. Season ticket loans are also available.
 
You are entitled to private healthcare, life cover, income protection, and eye
tests. You can also opt in to dental insurance.
 
We have enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental leave
policies in place. We also support our employees by offering an IVF, menopause,
baby loss, and trans equality policy.
 
Culture and wellbeing
We want everyone to feel like they belong at the Guardian and we champion
diversity of thought. Our various employee forums provide a platform to use
their voice to foster an inclusive workplace. We became the first major media
organisation to achieve B Corp status.
 
We offer tools to help you prioritise your wellbeing including access to our
employee benefits platform which provides tailored support for health and
wellbeing. In addition, we also offer free yoga and pilates classes. These run
alongside our corporate gym membership and cycle to work scheme.
 
Our canteen has views overlooking the Regents Canal and caters for breakfast,
lunch and dinner.
 
Learning and development
We encourage personal and professional growth. Employees have access to a broad
range of tools and solutions, and we are happy to support the pursuit of
professional qualifications through vocational courses and apprenticeships.
 
We value honesty in your application.
AI generated content must not be presented as your own work.

While the rest of the security industry obsesses over locking data down to prevent it from being lost or stolen, we're doing something fundamentally different at Virtru. We've created both a suite of powerful data protection applications and an open platform that's sparking an ecosystem of innovation. **Lead the operational backbone that a global portfolio of 20+ software businesses depends on.**
## **The Role**
Turner Portfolio is part of Volaris Group (Constellation Software). We acquire vertical market software businesses and hold them forever. Our Portfolio has 20+ businesses across 3 Verticals, spanning North America, EMEA and APAC.
We are looking for a Vice President, Portfolio Operations to own the operational and governance backbone the portfolio runs on: financial reporting and analysis, Investment Committee process, legal, information security, systems and data, and people support for the portfolio team.
This is a newly created role reporting directly to the Portfolio CEO. You will lead a nine-person team across five specialisms — financial reporting, legal, information security, systems and data, and people support — based in North America and Europe.
This is a strategic partner role. The reporting the Portfolio CEO takes outside the portfolio originates here. Operational excellence is the floor: we expect you to use that vantage point to spot and act on improvement opportunities across reporting, controls, data and operations.
Travel expectation is reasonably light and largely in your control. Attendance at the monthly portfolio leadership meeting in the UK is the one fixed commitment. Beyond that, you decide: portfolio or Volaris events, team-building, and the occasional visit where it earns its keep.
## **Where the role sits**
The Turner Portfolio leadership team reports to the Portfolio CEO, each role with a distinct remit:
* **Vertical CEOs** — grow their Verticals both organically and through acquisition
* **Chief Investment Officer** — the M&A engine, owning capital deployment and transactions
* **Chief Growth Officer** — the value creation engine, owning growth, capability and the growth operating model
* **VP, Portfolio Operations** — this role: the operational and governance hub the others depend on
The distinction matters: the Verticals own performance, the Chief Investment Officer deploys capital, the Chief Growth Officer creates value across the portfolio. You provide the reporting, governance, legal, security, systems and people infrastructure that lets all three move quickly and with confidence — deliberately lean, deliberately enabling. In practice that means light-touch reporting demands on the businesses, fast turnaround on compliance asks, and being generous with data and analytical support — an enabler, not a gatekeeper.
## **What you own**
* **Financial reporting and analysis.** Own the data, analysis and reporting the Portfolio CEO relies on outside the portfolio, consolidated with the Chief Growth Officer and Chief Investment Officer: quarterly strategic review packs, board packs and Volaris and Constellation Software submissions on time, every cycle, with variance commentary, trend analysis and leading indicators behind the numbers — plus internal control discipline, working capital cadence and consolidated cash flow visibility.
* **Investment Committee.** Run as a disciplined governance forum: fresh analysis, pre-reads in advance, decisions logged, actions tracked to completion.
* **Legal.** Deal support on acquisitions alongside the Chief Investment Officer, plus operational legal across commercial, employment, data and regulatory matters — pragmatic and low-friction for the businesses.
* **Information security and risk.** You own the posture and the outcomes — assessments, remediation, training and patch compliance; your security lead provides the technical depth.
* **Systems and data.** Own the portfolio's systems and data infrastructure: the shared backbone for the Chief Growth Officer's AI and operating model programmes and the Portfolio CEO's reporting, maintained for availability, integration health and data quality.
* **People support.** Serving a portfolio team of around 45 people across North America and Europe, with employment compliance and employee experience front of mind.
* **Team leadership.** Nine people across five specialisms. Recruit well, delegate properly, and address underperformance early.
## **You lead experts — you do not need to be one in every field**
The team you lead are capable specialists with real depth in their disciplines: legal, security, reporting, systems and people support. Your job is to set direction, ask the right questions, connect the functions, support your team and hold the standard. You are accountable for outcomes across all five areas, but you do not need to be the deepest expert in any of them — only literate enough in each to recognise when something needs attention.
## **What is in it for you**
Few roles at this level combine five functions with a genuine portfolio-wide view: 20+ businesses and more arriving via acquisition, close proximity to real capital allocation decisions, and a direct partnership with the Portfolio CEO from day one. This is a building role, not a caretaking one — use your experience and your ideas to make the portfolio run better. In turn, we will challenge and support you to be the best version of your professional self.
## **How we work**
We push ourselves and each other. We try things, we get some of them wrong, and we prefer that to standing still — which means we are willing to question how something has always been done and test a different route. Curiosity and a bit of healthy challenge go a long way here.
We are also straightforwardly human with each other: we care about people personally, we are honest when something is difficult, and we laugh a lot. Nobody carries a difficult week on their own here.
The standard is high and consistently applied. Reporting cycles do not move, the numbers are properly tested, and problems are better raised early than managed quietly. Stay composed when things compress, be direct about what is not working, and take a challenge on your work in your stride — do that, and you will find significant scope, considerable trust and very little bureaucracy.

* **Senior operations leader who has run a multi-function stack.** Likely backgrounds: VP or SVP of Portfolio Operations or Shared Services in a listed group, Director of Operations at a mid-cap software business, Group Operations Director or Chief of Staff with finance, legal and IT reporting in, or portfolio operations leadership within Volaris or Constellation Software.

* **Proven at leading functions outside your own expertise.** You have owned a discipline where your best report knew more than you did, and can evidence how you set the standard, read the signals and held a specialist to account — including hiring into disciplines whose craft you cannot assess hands-on.
* **Comfortable in a federated, decentralised operating model.**
* **Sufficient information security and risk literacy to own the posture.** You need not be a security practitioner, but you must be able to set the standard, interrogate the metrics and hold a dedicated specialist to account.

# Customer Host (4 HRS)
Please, note this role is a 4 hours contract and weekend availability may be required.
**WHO WE ARE**
White Stuff was established in 1985 through a simple idea. This idea grew and now we have shops and concessions in the UK and internationally, selling women’s and men’s clothing as well as beautiful accessories and homeware. Our original prints (all designed in house), intricate details and considered design touches reflect our personality and make us subtly distinctive.
Our people are at the heart of our brand, constantly moving and driving us forward. We’re sociable, talented and like minded and we’re not hierarchical or political in how we do business. We encourage entrepreneurial ideas and accountability at all levels.
**WHO YOU ARE**
You’ll be passionate about Retail and Fashion. You will have the determination to go the extra mile and provide the best customer experience. You will thrive in a team environment, and you will inspire others with your passion and support.
**PRIMARY OBJECTIVE OF THE JOB**
Ensure we are the best on the high street for delivering an amazing customer experience.
**WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING**
You’ll report to the Shop Manager and sit within our Retail team.
**Customer Experience**
* Meeting the A.C.E pillars (Be Friendly, Be Inspiring and Be Invaluable) throughout the Customer Journey.
* Holding an understanding of shop KPIs and working to continuously improve them.
* Promoting multichannel shopping by using the mobile point of sale system (mPOS) to show customers the products available across our channels and creating endless aisle orders.
* Engaging customers with our brand by signing customers up to email newsletters, tagging their purchases to their profile, and sending e-receipts in line with data protection regulations.
* Using knowledge of promotions or discounts available to inform our customers and increase sales.
* Assisting in events including Customer Event and preview evenings.
**Product Presentation and Visual Standards**
* Maintaining high visual standards instore.
* Supporting with floor moves, mannequin and window displays, and replenishment.
* Understanding the features (fits, style, fabrics) of our product ranges and explaining these to our customers to support their buying decisions.
**Shop Operations**
* Processing deliveries efficiently and ensuring that on the shop floor products are replenished and always available for customers
* Supporting in stock management processes such as stocktakes.
* Using company resources such as the White Stuff website, Looking White Stuff, the Tea Room, email communications, window guidelines and brand posts to engage with our customer and ensure compliance with daily/weekly actions.
* Being a team player and playing an active role in team briefs.
* Understanding and complying with the Health & Safety and emergency procedures in store.
* Having a professional approach to our internal customers, head office departments, centre management (where applicable) and any other visitors.
* Efficient and accurately fulfilling ship from store and Click + Collect processes.
**Doing Good Stuff**
* Holding an awareness of our charity partner and the positive impact this has including supporting any events or charity promotions.
* Understanding our approach to ethical sourcing and environmental impact to be able to explain this to our customers and the team.
**Benefits**
As a Customer Host at White Stuff you will be entitled to an array of great benefits, some of which include:
* Quarterly bonus opportunity
* Up to 25 days holiday per annum plus bank holidays
* 2 days paid (as per your contracted hours) per year to volunteer in the local community
* 50% product discount
* Annual uniform allowance
* BUPA Dental Insurance
* Healthcare cash plan and Life Assurance
* Interest free season ticket loan

# Senior Project Manager - Location Based Entertainment (LBE)
* Full-time
## Company Description
**Location:**183 Eversholt Street, London NW1 1BU, UK
**Hybrid work:** Employees work in a hybrid model balancing collaboration in our office and remote work.
**Overview**
WildBrain CPLG is a world-leading entertainment, sport and brand licensing agency with 20 offices worldwide. Since 1972 we have been providing our partners with dedicated licensing and marketing professionals and fully integrated retail, creative & product development, legal and accounting services.
We are looking to add to our talented team of innovators that can help us manage some of the most profitable and enduring brands in the world! We believe that our partnerships are about clarity, openness, and trust, and we are widely known for our straightforward approach.
**About the Role**
The Senior Project Manager (PM) will work directly with licensees, licensors, vendors, consultants, and internal stakeholders to oversee the creative development and execution of multiple Location-Based Entertainment (LBE), **live event, performance, and other offline experiential projects**, ensuring projects are delivered on brand, on schedule, and aligned with creative and commercial objectives.
The Senior PM will be responsible for managing project timelines, approvals, reporting, stakeholder coordination, and key delivery milestones across multiple projects and partners.
This role requires **proven experience managing offline experiential projects, events, performances, attractions, exhibitions, immersive experiences, or other guest-facing physical experiences,** strong project management capability, excellent communication skills, and the ability to manage complex experiential and IP-driven projects in a fast-paced international environment.
In addition to core project management responsibilities, the role will also support selected business development and account management activities, helping ensure continuity between commercial discussions and project execution.
## Job Description
* Lead the creative development process for LBE projects, working closely with internal teams and external partners to meet business objectives.
* Develop and manage project plans with internal teams, third-party vendors, and licensees, setting clear goals, deliverables, budgets, timelines, and responsibilities.
* Manage licensing partnerships, ensuring compliance with brand standards, approval processes, project schedules, and key deliverables.
* Identify, assess, and mitigate project risks to ensure projects stay on brand, on time, and on budget.
* Maintain strong working relationships and facilitate clear communication with licensors, licensees, design partners, vendors, consultants, and internal stakeholders across multiple territories and time zones.
* Provide relevant feedback, reviews, and approvals for creative submissions across entertainment, marketing, merchandising, retail, operational, and guest experience workstreams.
* Assist in vendor prequalification, selection, and evaluation, making recommendations as needed.
* Track progress and provide regular updates on project activities, including managing design reviews with various vendors and coordinating stakeholder feedback and approvals.
* Oversee the development of project processes, including responsibility assignment matrices (RACI), timelines, budgets, approvals, and other key documentation.
* Support project delivery and launch readiness coordination across creative, operational, and partner workstreams where required.
* Review and track IP approval processes to ensure compliance with all creative and licensing guidelines.
* Conduct post-project assessments to evaluate creative, process, and goal achievement.
* Assist in preparing presentations, project summaries, meeting materials, and internal reporting documentation.
* Work collaboratively with regional licensing teams to align project activity with broader commercial objectives.
## Qualifications
* **Bachelor’s degree and / or significant experience managing Location-Based Entertainment, themed entertainment, live events, performances, attractions, exhibitions, immersive experiences, hospitality, or other experiential projects, is essential.**
* Demonstrable track record of delivering physical, guest-facing experiences from concept through launch, including coordination of multiple stakeholders, vendors, and operational teams.
* Qualification in project management or equivalent professional experience in project management, themed entertainment, experiential, architecture, design, production, or related fields.
* Proven expertise in coordinating projects through development, approvals, delivery, and launch phases within partner-facing or client-facing environments.
* Experience working across licensors, licensees, operators, vendors, consultants, and cross-functional internal teams.
* Strong understanding of IP brand standards, approval processes, and experiential project delivery.
* Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to coordinate effectively across internal teams, licensors, partners, and external vendors.

London

### About YLD:
YLD is a software engineering and product design consultancy, founded in 2013, headquartered in London, with delivery teams in Lisbon and Porto.
We work with engineering and product leaders who know what good looks like and are frustrated by the gap between strategy and execution. We embed senior engineers and designers inside client teams, working in their codebase, their tooling, their delivery rhythm. AI runs through how our teams work, and we help clients adopt it into their own workflows too.
We have deep experience in regulated environments including financial services, payments, healthcare, and energy. Most of our client relationships run well beyond two years. Nearly all of our work comes through repeat business and referrals. We build things clients can own after we leave.
### About the role:
We're building out data as a first-class practice at YLD, and we need someone in London who can be the credible technical voice in front of clients and prospects, not just describing what we could do, but backing it with real delivery experience.
This is a senior role, reporting to our Head of Engineering. You'll sit alongside our commercial and client services leadership in meetings where technical credibility matters, help shape and win new engagements, and stay close enough to client work to guide it and step in yourself when an engagement needs you. Alongside, we expect you to build our external reputation in data through events, writing, and the wider community.
### About you:
You've been a strong data engineer or data lead for years, and you're comfortable in front of a client as well as in a pull request. You know what good data work looks like well enough to spot it, or its absence, in the first ten minutes of a client conversation. You've probably led a team before. Consultancy background is a strong plus, but not essential if you've got real client or stakeholder exposure elsewhere.
You don't need an existing public profile in the data community, but you'll need the appetite to build one and the technical depth to make it credible when you do.
### Your day-to-day responsibilities will look like this:
**Hands-on delivery (core, from day one)**
* Doing hands-on data engineering work directly, pipelines, transformation layers, models, and the infrastructure around them, not just guiding others
* Adapting to different client contexts: legacy warehouse migrations, greenfield lakehouses, transformation layers that need rescuing
* Guiding the wider team and unblocking hard technical problems as your remit grows beyond your own delivery
* Defining and evolving our internal standards for data work: testing, documentation, project structure, code review
* Mentoring and growing data engineers across the company
**Client and commercial (core, from day one)**
* Joining client and prospect meetings as the technical authority on data, alongside our client services and commercial leads
* Shaping proposals and pitches, translating client problems into a credible data approach and a defensible scope
* Acting as the escalation point on live data engagements when technical judgement calls need weight behind them
* Travelling to client sites for workshops, discovery sessions, and in-person relationship building, and representing YLD at external data events
**Practice, talent, and external profile (growth, over the first year)**
* Owning the growth of YLD's data practice: capability, reputation, and headcount over time
* Contributing to attracting and hiring strong data engineers into YLD
* Representing YLD at data events and in the wider community as your standing in the market builds
* Supporting our sales team so that data becomes something we can proactively sell, not just respond to
### You'll have the following skills and experience:
**Leadership and commercial**
* Consulting or agency experience is a strong plus, but real client or stakeholder-facing exposure elsewhere is acceptable
* A track record of technical leadership: leading a team or function
* Comfortable presenting to senior client stakeholders and holding your own under commercial pressure
* Cross-functional fluency: you translate engineering constraints into business terms and negotiate realistic commitments
* Appetite to build a public presence in the data community over time, even if you don't have one yet
**Technical**
Not theoretical, evidenced by things you've actually shipped, and deep enough to set the bar for a team and answer a sceptical client:
* SQL as engineering: read and review SQL that performs at scale, and understand query planning, engine quirks, and how materialisation choices affect cost and performance well enough to guide a team's decisions
* Python for data: built and maintained production data systems in typed, testable Python, not just notebooks, and can set that standard for others
* Data modelling: made deliberate choices between dimensional, Data Vault, normalised and denormalised designs, and can explain the trade-offs in flexibility, query performance, and maintainability to both engineers and clients
* Transformation architecture: design transformations that are idempotent, incremental, and dependency-aware. You think in DAGs, not scripts
* Pipeline design: weigh batch, streaming, and micro-batch trade-offs against latency, complexity, cost, and reprocessability, and pick the right approach for the problem
* Data testing: know what to catch at build time (schema contracts, assertions, transformation logic) versus defer to observability, and can make that call for a team
* Data observability: treat data reliability like site reliability, with measurable indicators, alerting, incident response, and root cause analysis
* CI/CD for data: version, test, and deploy pipelines like software, with environment promotion, rollback strategies, and infrastructure as code
* Data governance: implemented lineage, cataloguing, sensitive data classification, or access control, and can hold a client to account on making data auditable and secure
* Cost-conscious: optimised warehouse spend, storage strategies, or job efficiency, and treat compute as a resource to manage, not ignore
* Platform fluency: worked across orchestration (Airflow, Dagster), warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks), ingestion (Fivetran, Airbyte, custom), and transformation (dbt, Spark)
* AI Native: experienced in agentic coding workflows (context, harness, loop, and graph engineering), and able to embed AI Engineering constructs into pipelines (RAG, semantic search, evals, guardrails, etc)
## **You should apply if:**
* Confident and credible in front of clients and prospects, without needing a script, and comfortable holding a firm technical or commercial line when a client or prospect pushes back
* Still able to hold up in a deep technical review today, architecture, data modelling, pipeline design, not just talk about decisions you made a few years ago

Milo is an AI-powered data analyst that enables teams to get reliable answers from their business data in minutes. # Senior Pricing Manager- PCI
**Hybrid**Underwriting and Pricing
London, England, United Kingdom
## Description
### About Zego
Insurance hasn't changed much in over a century. The way we live, work and travel has.
Good drivers are the entire point of Zego. Seven in 10 drivers on the road are consistently good, but until telematics came along there was no way to prove it, so nearly everyone paid a price based on averages. Zego is the company built to change that.
At Zego, we're leading the AI evolution in insurance.
We move fast, without the layers that usually slow things down. AI takes the routine work off every team, from Finance to Product to Marketing, so people ship real code and launch custom dashboards in minutes. Engineering commits are entirely AI-assisted, which shifts the focus from team size to the quality of your thinking, and our data warehouse connects directly to an AI assistant for instant answers. Backed by a modern tech stack (Claude Code, Snowflake, Figma and Zapier) and a commitment to adopting new tools in days rather than quarters, you get complete ownership to do the most impactful work of your career.
### Purpose of the role
As Senior Pricing Manager at Zego, you will be a key leader within the PCI pricing function, responsible for shaping and executing pricing strategy across Personal Car products, markets, and customer segments. You will own complex pricing decisions end to end, balancing growth, profitability, and customer value, while ensuring pricing remains aligned with Zego's broader commercial and strategic objectives.
Operating at senior level, you will act as a strategic partner to leadership, influence company wide decision making, and help scale pricing capability as Zego continues to grow in the UK and Europe. You will set direction, provide thought leadership, and raise the standard of pricing across the organisation.
### What you will be doing
* Partner with the Director of Pricing and senior leadership to define and execute pricing strategy that supports growth, profitability, and long term value creation.
* Own end to end pricing for a portfolio of products or initiatives, from strategic design through to launch, monitoring, and optimisation.
* Lead pricing decisions for new propositions, market entries, and major commercial changes, ensuring clear rationale, governance, and alignment with business goals.
* Develop and evolve pricing frameworks, methodologies, and performance metrics that can scale with the business.
* Provide clear commercial insight and recommendations through data driven analysis, translating complex pricing outcomes into actionable decisions for non technical stakeholders.
* Act as a thought leader for pricing, challenging existing approaches, driving innovation, and raising pricing maturity across the organisation.
* Mentor and develop other pricing team members, contributing to capability building, best practice, and a high performance culture.
### What you will need to be successful
* Significant experience in Personal or Commercial Lines pricing, commercial strategy, or revenue management, with demonstrated ownership of complex pricing decisions in a fast paced environment.
* You've owned work from data through to deployment, worked with high-volume data and drove decisions independently.
* You've advanced analytical capability and comfort working with data driven insights, models, and performance metrics, regardless of specific tools or languages used.
* Excellent communication and storytelling skills, able to simplify complexity and influence decision making at executive level.
* Autonomy in a smaller setup and experience building, scaling, or improving pricing frameworks, governance, or operating models.
* Demonstrated people leadership or coaching experience, with a track record of developing others and elevating team performance.
* You work AI-first. You will use AI daily here, and we mean daily. You do not need to arrive an expert, but you do need to arrive curious, experiment fast, and take ownership of getting good quickly. People who wait to be trained will find this uncomfortable.
### What it's like to work at Zego
At Zego, we operate like a high-performing sports team. We come together as one, driven by ambition, backed by real support, and united by a shared mission to win.
Working here means having the backing, the coaching, and an inclusive community of Zegons across the UK and Europe who celebrate your wins and raise your game. It also means holding ourselves to high standards: moving with urgency, taking complete ownership, and embracing honest feedback that helps us continuously learn and evolve.
This is your opportunity for a career-defining experience, and one you will own.
.
### The Zego ways of working
Teams work better with time to collaborate and space to get things done. We call it Zego Hybrid: some of us are in our central London office weekly, others monthly or quarterly. It is about finding the balance between face time and focus that produces great work and a healthy life around it.
We also make a point of getting everyone in the same room. Teams come together every quarter, and once a year the whole company does, properly. It is a serious investment and consistently one of the best parts of the year...

Insurance hasn't changed much in over a century. The way we live, work and travel has.
